A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Omni-Attribute work. All 21 pages, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original personalization comparisons, human evaluations, ablations, embedding analyses, retrieval results, and qualitative applications, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the quantitative evaluations in Tables 1 and 3 and the supplementary qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The annotation pipeline, attribute encoder, generative and contrastive objectives, decoder, and compositional inference procedure are unchanged. Revised descriptions clarify the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the nine training datasets, 15-attribute personalization benchmark, Animal Dataset embedding analysis, CelebA retrieval, and supplementary application scenarios. The corrected sample total does not change coverage.

E2.justification: Personalization comparisons retain CLIP, DINOv2, Qwen-VL, OmniGen2, FLUX-Kontext, and Qwen-Image-Edit. Retrieval retains the GPT-4o plus CLIP baseline. Bibliography changes do not alter evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 revises the reported benchmark size from 350 to 375 samples and human ratings from 10.5K to 11.25K. Both versions already specify 15 attributes, five images and five prompts per attribute, and ten participants. These are reporting corrections; the PDFs do not establish additional evaluation or reruns.

E4.justification: Table 1 retains the same architecture, training, and contrastive-hyperparameter ablations. Composition demonstrations, embedding visualizations, retrieval analyses, and appendix case studies are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Scoring and averaging practices remain unchanged; the revised rating total concerns sample accounting.

E6.justification: All numerical results in Tables 1 and 3 match, and the plotted results and qualitative examples are unchanged. The revised sample and rating totals concern evaluation settings rather than empirical outcomes.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), the similarity and pooling definitions, and the compositional velocity construction are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about an open-vocabulary attribute encoder, dual-objective learning, disentanglement, composability, and downstream performance.

C2.justification: The results interpretations and limitations concerning image editing, correlated attributes, and contrastive hyperparameter sensitivity remain the same. Revised ablation wording restates the existing interpretation that models without contrastive learning fail to distinguish attribute conditions.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hardware, training schedules, annotation procedures, and the project link are retained. FLUX.1-dev identification moves from Appendix A.3 prose into its architecture table; it was already disclosed in v1.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography add Canvas-to-Image and Alchemint while removing Omni-ID and ComposeMe. Additional citations support existing passages, but the overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Limited edits refine introductory wording, contrastive-learning explanations, compositional score terminology, and ablation descriptions. An author's displayed name is reordered. The section and appendix structure is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 7 moves from the right to the left column on page 7, with accompanying text reflow. Figure 10's caption changes a single positive attribute to one or a few, matching the existing Appendix A.1 description. No result figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves the benchmark-size inconsistency: 15 attributes with 25 samples each yield 375, not 350, and the stated rating total is adjusted accordingly. Caption and wording refinements also improve consistency. These are limited reporting improvements; the method, empirical evidence, and conclusions remain unchanged.
